notes: Account summary: Argentum Pillar is a legaltech platform with a large litigation archive; currently uses a self-hosted vector DB for embeddings + a heuristics-based scorer.
Primary goal: migrate embeddings + reranker to reduce cost/query and improve top-K relevance for retrieval-augmented workflows across 30M documents.
Scale: expect 20k QPS/day peak, 150k daily queries, index size ~30M docs (~120M vectors with metadata). Concern about indexing time and incremental reindexing window.
Latency targets: synchronous query median <120ms, p95 <400ms for retrieval + rerank pipeline; offline batch embedding throughput target also important.
Cost sensitivity: high — current cost per query ~ $0.20; target <$0.05/token-equivalent with quantized models and batching.
Model preferences: lean toward open Llama2/Redwood-verified models for embeddings; prefer smaller reranker that supports quantization and GPU throughput.
Routing/fallback: need policy for fallback to cheaper model variant during peak and regional routing to NA data centers; automated A/B and canary rollouts required.

Eval concerns: strong emphasis on eval-driven migration — cannot accept regressions vs current production reranker. Request: Redwood evals harness + golden prompt set and automated metric diff reports.
Security: must integrate with corporate SSO (SAML), KMS for key management, and produce audit logs for queries (30-day retention). Data residency: NA-only until legal signoff.
Quote from Head of Search: 'We will not ship unless the reranker shows no regression on our litigation precision metrics — false positives cost us billable hours.'
Docs shared: POC ingestion scripts, baseline eval set (5k queries + relevance judgments), current reranker model weights (for back-compat tests).
Internal sentiment: engineering likes Redwood's batching & caching; security is cautious — legal team needs explicit retention controls. Finance pushing for conservative ARR commitment.
